title: Blinded disputers do not cancel Scripture light for sincere Spirit-led readers
source_text: XLVIII. Igitur si veritas aliqua dubia redditur, & probatio aliqua infirmatur, quia multi sunt qui lucem istius veritatis, & probationis vim non vident & agnoscunt, sed contra ex iisdem principiis disputant, & utcunque solvunt argumenta ex illis pro veritate adducta, nullum prorsus Dei verbum supererit, unde satis solide possint haeretici confutari, & dogmata fidei probari satis certo atque evidenter. Sed profecto quamvis homines praejudiciis & pravis affectibus ducti & occaecati doctrinam salutarem in Scriptura sacra contentam non videant, & argutiis ac vanis sophismatis tenebras illi offundere conentur, id non obstat, quominus illam ex Scripturis evidenter colligant, & firma ac indubitata illius argumenta se in iis habere certi sint illi qui animo sincero, & mente a praejudiciis & affectibus perversis libera, ac Spiritu sancto duce, & facem praeferente, Scripturae testimonia expendunt, & conferunt ut veritatem in illis inveniant.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore if some truth is rendered doubtful, and some proof is weakened, because there are many who do not see and acknowledge the light of that truth and the force of the proof, but on the contrary dispute from the same principles, and somehow solve the arguments drawn from them for the truth, there will remain absolutely no word of God whence heretics can be solidly enough confuted, and the dogmas of the faith proved sufficiently certainly and evidently. But indeed although men led and blinded by prejudices and wicked affections do not see the saving doctrine contained in sacred Scripture, and strive by subtleties and vain sophisms to pour darkness upon it, that does not hinder that those who with a sincere mind, and a mind free from prejudices and perverse affections, and with the Holy Spirit as guide and torchbearer, weigh and compare the testimonies of Scripture so as to find the truth in them, evidently gather that doctrine from the Scriptures, and are certain that they have in them its firm and undoubted arguments.
pass_b_english: If many dispute the same proofs made every rule useless, no word of God could ever settle heresy.
Prejudice and vain sophisms can darken Scripture for the blinded — that does not cancel its light.
Sincere minds, freed from perverse affections and led by the Spirit, still gather the saving doctrine evidently from Scripture.
They hold firm, undoubted arguments in the text itself.

lemmas.gloss: with the Holy Spirit as guide and torchbearer
